name: Hirschsprung Disease-Ganglioneuroblastoma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Hirschsprung Disease-Ganglioneuroblastoma Syndrome

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of aganglionosis in the distal colon
Histological confirmation of ganglioneuroblastoma tumor presence
Clinical signs of intestinal obstruction including chronic constipation and abdominal distension
Identification of pathogenic variants in RET proto-oncogene or related genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of histopathological aganglionosis and histological confirmation of ganglioneuroblastoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, clinical presentation, and genetic testing.

laboratory: Elevated urinary catecholamines (VMA, HVA) in ganglioneuroblastoma
Electrolyte imbalances due to bowel obstruction
imaging: Contrast enema demonstrating transition zone in colon
MRI or CT scan identifying tumor extent and metastasis
other: Histopathology confirming absence of ganglion cells in bowel biopsy
Histological identification of ganglioneuroblastoma tumor cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of malignant neuroblastoma without intestinal aganglionosis
Different tumor histology and clinical presentation

redFlags: Failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth
Signs of enterocolitis with fever and sepsis
references: Amiel J, Lyonnet S. Hirschsprung disease, associated syndromes, and genetics: a review. J Med Genet. 2001;38(11):729-739.
Maris JM. Recent advances in neuroblastoma. N Engl J Med. 2010;362(23):2202-2211.
Orphanet Report Series. Hirschsprung disease-ganglioneuroblastoma syndrome. Orphanet; 2024.
